subject: Locked out
body: My account is locked after too many login attempts. How do I get back in?

kb_articles.content:
Why your account is locked

This article is for anyone who is shut out of their account after several unsuccessful attempts to sign in.

Accounts lock after 5 failed login attempts within 15 minutes. Lockout clears automatically after 1 hour.

What this means for you: if you try to log in and fail 5 times within a 15 minute window, the account is locked and you cannot get in for a while. This is a temporary lockout, not a permanent block. You do not need to do anything to undo it, because the lockout clears automatically after 1 hour. Once that hour has passed, the account is available again and you can try to log in as usual. The rule counts failed login attempts over a 15 minute window, and the lock applies once there have been 5 of them inside that window. Fewer than 5 failed attempts within 15 minutes does not lock the account. Failed two-factor authentication codes count as failed login attempts, so entering a wrong 2FA code 5 times within 15 minutes also locks the account.

draft:
Thank you for getting in touch.

As you've been locked out after too many login attempts, here's what you need to know: accounts lock automatically after 5 failed login attempts within a 15-minute window. The good news is that this lockout clears automatically after 1 hour — you don't need to take any action to unlock it. Once the hour has passed, you'll be able to log in as normal.

It's also worth knowing that failed two-factor authentication codes count as failed login attempts, so if you use 2FA, incorrect codes contributed to the lockout in the same way.

If you're still unable to access your account after the hour has passed, please don't hesitate to get back in touch and we'll be happy to help further.

This article is for anyone who has forgotten their password, does not remember it, or wants to set a new one.

To reset a password, use the 'Forgot password' link on the login page. Reset emails expire after 30 minutes.

What this means for you: if you cannot sign in because you do not remember your password, start from the login page and select the 'Forgot password' link. The reset is done through an email, and that email stops working after 30 minutes, so it is best to open it as soon as it arrives. If more than 30 minutes have passed, the email can no longer be used to reset the password. In that case, use the 'Forgot password' link on the login page again.

subject: when do you charge me
body: signed up on the 17th, what date does my card get hit each month?

kb_articles.content:
When you are billed

This article is for customers who want to know when their subscription payment is taken each month, and how refunds are worked out.

Billing occurs on the same calendar day each month as the original signup date. Refunds are prorated.

What this means for you: the date you first signed up decides your billing date. For example, if you signed up on the 12th, you are billed on the 12th of every month after that. The charge does not move around from month to month. When a refund is given, it is prorated, which means the amount is worked out proportionally and not as a flat figure. If you are not sure which day your billing date falls on, look at the day you originally signed up. This also applies to plan changes made part of the way through a billing period: the difference is prorated.

draft:

subject: stop my subscription
body: Want to cancel, not using it anymore. where do I do that?

kb_articles.content:
How to cancel your subscription

This article is for customers who want to end their subscription, stop their plan or unsubscribe.

Subscriptions can be cancelled anytime from Account Settings > Billing. Access continues until the end of the current billing period; no partial refunds are issued for early cancellation.

What this means for you: you can cancel whenever you like, and you do it yourself in Account Settings > Billing. After you cancel, you keep your access until the end of the billing period you are currently in. Cancelling part of the way through a billing period does not earn a partial refund for the rest of it. Because access continues until the end of the current billing period, cancelling does not cut your access off straight away. Early cancellation means cancelling before that billing period has ended, and no partial refunds are issued in that case. The no-partial-refunds rule applies only to cancelling a subscription; plan changes made part of the way through a billing period are covered in the billing cycle article.

draft:
Thank you for getting in touch.

You can cancel your subscription at any time by going to **Account Settings > Billing**. Once cancelled, your access will continue until the end of your current billing period. Please note that no partial refunds are issued for early cancellation.

kb_articles.content:
Two-factor authentication (2FA)

This article is for customers who want to turn on two-factor authentication, and for customers who can no longer use their 2FA device.

Two-factor authentication can be enabled in Account Settings > Security. If a user loses access to their 2FA device, support can issue a temporary bypass code after identity verification.

What this means for you: to add this extra layer of sign-in protection, turn on two-factor authentication in Account Settings > Security. If you lose the device you use for 2FA, or otherwise cannot get to it, the way back in is a temporary bypass code. Support can issue that code, and only after your identity has been verified. The code is temporary, and identity verification comes first. Turning two-factor authentication on is something you do yourself in the Security section of your account settings.
